01Rationale

Why this level matters

Coding agents write much of the code now, so the lasting skills are specifying clearly, testing thoroughly and understanding what you ship. This course teaches full-stack development with an agent as a working partner, and no-code tools where they are enough.

02Target competencies

Intended learning outcomes

Specify clearly

Write specs and tests an AI agent can build from.

Build full-stack

Create a working web app with a front end, back end and database.

Ship it

Deploy, monitor and update a product people can use.

Stay in control

Review, test and understand every change an agent makes.

Proposed scope: 16 lessons in 4 modules

This outline describes the intended curriculum. Lesson materials and assessments are not yet available.

Module 1Foundations

The ground you stand on.

  1. Python programming
  2. Web basics: HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  3. Databases and APIs
  4. Git and working in a team

Module 2Building with AI

A coding agent as a partner.

Module 3Full-stack products

From page to product.

Module 4Shipping

Make it real.

  1. Deployment

  4. Your launch plan

04Planned practical work

A small SaaS product, shipped

Proposed project: Build and deploy a small product with a coding agent, from spec to live users. This practical component will be developed and validated before the level opens.

The steps

  1. Write the one-page spec
  2. Write the first tests
  3. Build the back end with your agent
  4. Build the front end
  5. Deploy it
  6. Write the readme and the launch plan

Intended validation criteria

  • Every feature has a test
  • You can explain each file the agent wrote
  • The deployed app has a working sign-in

05How you learn

Proposed learning design

Worked examples

The professional academies begin with complete examples and make the reasoning behind good decisions visible.

Guided practice

Scaffolds fade as learners progress—from annotated examples to structured tasks and independent work.

Retrieval and review

Low-stakes questions prompt recall; review revisits important concepts. Model answers and rubrics make improvement specific.

Research-informed updates

The academies cite primary research and standards, record review dates and receive versioned updates as evidence changes.

The proposed learning design draws on retrieval practice, worked examples and spaced review; detailed learner materials will be published before release. Read the evidence and sources.

06Intended audience

What you need

No experience needed for the early lessons. You should be comfortable installing software.
